intent: The heading that gives its Dialog's popup its accessible name.
typical_uses: The one heading of a dialog, stating the task it holds

dont_use_when.situation: The heading of a card on the page

invariants.text: DialogTitle renders an h2 set in the heading-2 type ramp with no margin.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a second DialogTitle in the same popup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep one DialogTitle per dialog and use plain headings for any subheadings; the popup's `aria-labelledby` points at one title's id

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the title's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the title's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dialog.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A plain heading in place of DialogTitle
bad.why: A plain heading carries no id the primitive knows about, so the popup gets no `aria-labelledby` and a screen reader announces an unnamed dialog.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DialogTitleState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: DialogTitleState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the title's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dialog.module.css, not through this.
